﻿# 意外成为创始人，连续两年成功退出

## 冷启动：他做产品只是为了练手

Sharath accidentally became founder。

2018年开始 building products。

But goal was launch on PH — that's it。

No intention of monetizing。

Just wanted to build founder muscle。

But in 2020，when launched Shoutout's landing page。

People started saying they would pay for it。

So built MVP using no-code tools。

Validated idea。

Found tech co-founder online。

Grew to $40K ARR。

Sold for between $110K-$150K。

All while working full-time job。

Recently，sold second SaaS product GuestLab AI。

Small sale，only about $200 MRR。

Sold for $3.2K。

## 反直觉：先做受众，再做产品

This year，took leap and left full-time job。

To pay bills，started doing consulting work。

Difficult to find gigs。

So decided to start newsletter called Fractional Gigs。

Tweeted about it and good friend Alex DM'd saying should collab。

Alex started Founder Gigs in 2021 and sold it。

But then got assets back and wanted to launch it again。

So teamed up and launched in July。

Combining ideas。

Now，Founder Gigs is weekly newsletter。

Sources fractional gigs for ex-founders and startup operators。

Set up on beehiiv because wanted to launch quickly。

Now have more than 5K subs。

Made more than $1K in sponsorship revenue。

Also offer $5 monthly subscriptions unlocking exclusive fractional roles。

Currently at $74 MRR。

## 暴击：增长就是关注人

Here's what he learned from growing Shoutout：

**Grow an audience：**

Build audience before building product。

Can't tell how much he preaches and lives this ideology！

When launched Shoutout，had decent audience on Twitter。

Helped validate idea，get initial feedback，eventually gave push to build MVP！

**Build in public：**

Build aggressively in public。

With Shoutout，transparent from day zero。

Resulted in building solid community、momentum、so much word of mouth。

Hands down，best way to earn trust is by being transparent and doing things in public。

It's unlock and unfair advantage not every founder tapped into。

**Focus on customer service：**

Your users are kings and queens。

Instead of scheming how to win，always focus on how can create value for users。

In way，removes lot of pressure and allows be creative！

Doing insane customer service also one of best ways to win trust。

Be available to them and genuinely do things that add value。

Treat them equally。

They sense care and reflect it out in public。

**Focus on distribution channels：**

To keep momentum alive，keep targeting channels like Product Hunt、Indie Hackers、HN、Reddit。

Soft launch on Twitter first followed by launching on these channels。

More eyeballs，more chance for growth。

**Keep your momentum：**

Once have momentum，keep it。

Momentum is oxygen for any startup。

##  punchline：失败可以，但要不怕失败

Here's his advice：

Put every ounce of energy and focus into not failing。

But don't be afraid to fail！

Make speed friend so can build ridiculous momentum。

Build personal brand from Day 1。

It's massive advantage to have presence on internet。

Trust yourself。

He wishes hadn't doubted himself so much when started。

Self doubt drains energy and points in wrong direction。

Other than that，remember don't need to figure out everything before start。

Just start！
